call_goal: Learn whether Brambleton Bank has a real problem with its KYC summary assistant, why now, and who else cares
desired_outcomes: Their top problems in their words

transcript.text: So the assistant reads the ID and proof-of-address documents and drafts the KYC summary, and an analyst checks it. The slow bit is the analysts double-checking everything, because they don't trust the summaries yet.
What would make them trust it more?
Knowing why it said what it said, I think. Right now if an auditor asks why a file was approved, we can't show what the assistant looked at. That's the bit that worries compliance.
Paul Nyberg, he runs model risk. He's been asking for an audit trail since the pilot.
How many files go through the assistant a week?
Around four thousand, and more once we add business accounts next year.
And how long does an analyst check take?
Ten, fifteen minutes. Without the assistant it was about forty.
What happens when the summary's wrong?
The analyst fixes it, and nobody upstream hears about it. We don't keep track of the fixes anywhere.
Our data science team, three people, with an outside partner for the document reading part.
For the document model, yes. The summary part is all ours now.

unacceptable_behaviors: Asks another discovery question with about 9 minutes left and no next step
Books a meeting without playing back what they said first (weak, not wrong)
Pressure or urgency lines to get the meeting
Plays back pain they didn't name
acceptable_questions: From what you said: audit trail and untracked fixes. Book a session with Paul?
Can we book a follow-up with you and Paul next week?
